subject: Clarify: snapshot retention vs backup purge / cross-region deletion propagation
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@acme-corp.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: LegalOps <legalops@acme-corp.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Apr 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Snapshot/backup question for procurement review

Hi Naomi —

Quick question as we go through procurement: can you confirm how Redwood treats deletions for customer data relative to backups and snapshots? Specifically:

- If a user or tenant requests full deletion (and we issue a deletion API call), how long could their data still exist in backups/snapshots?
- Are backups retained in the same region as the primary data (data residency), or can they be replicated out-of-region?
- Does a deletion request trigger any immediate purge from backups, or is it handled via retention windows/lifecycles only?

LegalOps is looking for language we can include in the contract redlines. A plain-English timeline would be great.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Head of IT, Acme Corp
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, LegalOps <legalops@acme-corp.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Apr 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Snapshot/backup question for procurement review

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front, then a slightly more detailed explanation you can drop into contract language if helpful.

Short answers:
- Backups/snapshots: retained according to the customer-configurable retention policy (default 30 days). Deletion requests do NOT immediately scrub historical backups — they follow retention lifecycle.
- Residency: backups are by default stored in the same cloud region as primary data. Cross-region replication only happens if the customer enables DR replication.
- Immediate purges: we do not purge backups instantly on a standard deletion request due to safety & restore guarantees. We support a "legal purge" workflow for approved compliance requests (see below).

Draft contract-friendly wording we use internally: "Customer data deleted via the Redwood deletion API will be removed from live service storage immediately. Historical backups and snapshots are retained according to the configured retention period and will be overwritten or purged according to the backup lifecycle. Redwood will not proactively purge backup copies outside of the configured retention window except where required by a valid legal or compliance request."

More context and action items below — looping in Michael and Karthik for technical and SOC2 notes.

Best,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Snapshot/backup question for procurement review

Jordan, Naomi —

Adding the technical details to Naomi's summary so your infra team has the specifics:

How backups/snapshots work (high level):
- We take incremental snapshots of model state and customer blobs (tokens/meta) every 6 hours by default; full snapshots occur weekly.
- Snapshots are stored as object versions in the region's object store (encrypted at rest with KMS).
- Retention is implemented via lifecycle policies. Default TTL is 30 days; customers can request 90/180/365-day tiers on Dedicated/Private plans.

Deletion behavior:
- Live delete: when a deletion API call is accepted, the live service removes pointers and revokes access immediately.
- Backup copies: historical snapshots remain until TTL expiry. Because snapshots are incremental and often reference shared chunk objects, we can't reliably remove a tenant's bytes from older snapshots without rehydrating and reconstructing every affected snapshot — that is why we use lifecycle expiry rather than immediate purge.
- Legal/compliance purge: for approved legal orders, Redwood performs an expedited purge workflow: we identify affected object versions and trigger a forced deletion + overwrite where storage provider supports it. This process is auditable and can take up to 14 days depending on replication state and cloud provider guarantees.

Residency and replication:
- Default: backups colocated in the same region.
- DR replication: if you opt into cross-region DR, snapshots are replicated to the configured secondary region(s). Replication can be disabled for customers requiring strict single-region residency.

Restore window: restores from snapshots can be requested up to the retention TTL; for legal purge events, we will coordinate the earliest permissible restore point that excludes purged data.

I can attach a short diagram of the flow (where backup objects live and how lifecycle/purge runs).

—Michael

Quick compliance notes to add to contract bullets: 
- SOC 2: our audit scope covers backup processes, retention policies, and access controls. We maintain immutable audit logs showing when retention/purge jobs ran and who initiated expedited purges.
- Certification / evidence: we can provide a redacted sample audit extract and a statement of process for the legal purge workflow.
- SLA-related: expedited purge is treated as an operational request and not covered by uptime SLA; we will provide an ETA in the escalation path.

If you want, LegalOps can run a tabletop with our security team to sign off wording.
